# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.
I'll start by exploring the codebase to understand the transaction labeling logic.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.spatial.distance import pdist, squareform
from Levenshtein import jaro_winkler, distance
from scipy.cluster.hierarchy import linkage, cut_tree, dendrogram
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import traceback


def getmode(txn):
    unique_amount_df = txn.amount.unique()
    txn.reset_index().set_index('amount').loc[unique_amount_df, 'index'].values
    return 


def salary_detection(transactions):
    try:
        #assign empty string to cells with null values
        transactions['partyName'] = transactions['partyName'].fillna("")

        #grouping of data by similar party names
        STOP_WORDS_PARTYNAME = "privatelimited|private|limited|pvtltd"
        transactions['party2'] = transactions['partyName'].replace(to_replace=" ", value="", regex=True).str.lower().replace(to_replace=STOP_WORDS_PARTYNAME, value="", regex=True).str.strip()
        # grouping using clustering
        distance_matrix = squareform(pdist(transactions['party2'].values.reshape(-1,1), lambda x, y : distance(x[0], y[0])))
        
        # For testing purpose only
        # dend = dendrogram(linkage(distance_matrix, method  = "complete"))
        # plt.title('Dendrogram')
        # plt.xlabel('Customers')
        # plt.ylabel('Euclidean distances')
        # plt.show()
        
        transactions['Group_ID'] = cut_tree(linkage(distance_matrix, method='complete'), height=1.5)

        #finding the probable salary txns set
        NOT_SALARY = "XX4700.*Mobi|Mobi.*XX4700|credit card/|Deposit / Investment|MOB/TPFT/"
        LOAN_POSITIVE = "\\binsta\\s?loan|SHUBHLOANS|DISBUR-|\\besloan|\\bloan\\b|disbur\\s?s|disbur|disbu\\b|cashbean fund tr|NODAL A/C|NODAL Ac|NODALAC|KisshtFund|NODAL A C|ICICI BANK NODA"
        EXCLUDE_DEPOSIT = "CASH_DEPOSIT|FIXED_DEPOSIT|SELF_DEPOSIT|CASH_DEPOSIT_CHARGES|DEPOSITORY_CHARGES|FLEXI_DEPOSIT|INTEREST_ON_DEPOSIT|RECURRING_DEPOSIT"   # All the deposits except cheque deposit will be excluded from salary txn
       
        # filtering out txns to create sub txn dataframe for salary detection
        transactions_sub = transactions[transactions['type'].eq("CREDIT") & transactions['description'].notnull() & transactions['amount'].gt(2999)]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['transactionSubcategory'].isin(["INTERNAL_PAYMENT", "INVESTMENT_INCOME", "TRANSFER_FROM_WALLET", "EMI_MORATORIUM", "RENT", "REIMBURSEMENT", "SUBSIDIES", "RENT_INCOME"])]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['merchantType'].isin(["Pension"])]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['transactionCategory'].isin(["CASHBACK", "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE", "BANK_ACCOUNT_CLOSURE", "UPI", "IMPS","AUTO_SWEEP"])]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['transactionCategory'].str.contains("REVERSAL|RETURN|INTEREST|REFUND|CANCEL", na=False)]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['transactionCategory'].str.contains(EXCLUDE_DEPOSIT, na = False, case=False)]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['description'].str.contains(LOAN_POSITIVE, na=False, case=False)]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~transactions_sub['description'].str.contains(NOT_SALARY, na=False, case=False)]
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[transactions_sub['partyName'].str.len().gt(0) & transactions_sub['partyName'].notnull()]

        # remove txns with salary amount more than 30000 and divisible by 10000
        transactions_sub = transactions_sub[~(transactions_sub['amount'].gt(30000) & transactions['amount'].mod(10000).eq(0))]
        
        #transforming date into YYYY-MM form

from categorizationapp import app

client = app.test_client()

def run(bank, acc_type, txns, holder=""):
    payload = {
        "bank": bank, "acc_type": acc_type, "accountUID": "acc-1",
        "accountHolder": holder, "transactions": txns,
    }
    r = client.post('/categorizeTransaction', json=payload)
    d = r.get_json()
    if 'response' not in d:
        return d
    return d['response']

def txn(desc, amount, ttype, remark="", date="05/01/2022", bal=100000):
    return {"description": desc, "amount": amount, "type": ttype, "remark": remark,
            "transactionDate": date, "balanceAfterTransaction": bal}

def show(title, rows, fields=("description", "remark", "transactionCategory",
                              "transactionSubcategory", "partyName")):
    print("=" * 100)
    print(title)
    if isinstance(rows, dict):
        print("   ERROR:", rows); return
    for r in rows:
        print("   " + " | ".join(f"{f}={r.get(f)!r}" for f in fields))

# 1) HDFC: credit whose reference note (remark) is a long all-numeric string -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
show("1. HDFC credit, remark = 16-char all-numeric padded cheque ref",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("SOME NARRATION WITHOUT KEYWORDS", 25000, "CREDIT", remark="0000000000012345")]))

# 2) HDFC: salary credit whose narration is a bare numeric code -> SALARY sub-tag
show("2. HDFC credit, narration = bare 6-digit code (SAVING)",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("123456", 45000, "CREDIT", remark="X1")]))

# 3) ICICI: transfer narration opening with a direction word ahead of the name
show("3. ICICI TRFR TO:/TRFR FROM: narration",
     run("ICICI", "SAVING", [txn("TRFR TO:RAHUL KUMAR SHARMA", 5000, "DEBIT", remark="r1"),
                             txn("TRFR FROM:MEENA TRADERS", 7000, "CREDIT", remark="r2")]))

# 4) ICICI: 4-field slash-delimited bill transfer -> payee is the final field
show("4. ICICI BIL/INFT four-field reference",
     run("ICICI", "SAVING", [txn("BIL/INFT/12345/ANIL ELECTRICALS", 3000, "DEBIT", remark="r3")]))

# 5) HDFC: offsetting credit immediately after its matching debit -> REVERSAL (not bounce)
show("5. HDFC offsetting credit right after matching debit (same IMPS narration)",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("IMPS-123456789-SOMEONE-HDFC-XXXXXX-PAYMENT", 8000, "DEBIT", remark="a", date="03/01/2022"),
                            txn("IMPS-123456789-SOMEONE-HDFC-XXXXXX-PAYMENT", 8000, "CREDIT", remark="b", date="03/01/2022")]))

# --- regression probes: rows that were already correct must not shift ---
show("R1. HDFC ordinary UPI debit",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("UPI-JOHN DOE-JOHNDOE@OKAXIS-XXXX-123-PAYMENT", 500, "DEBIT", remark="12345678")]))
show("R2. HDFC 16-digit remark transfer, non-zero prefix (stays TRANSFER)",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("SOME NARRATION", 900, "CREDIT", remark="1234567890123456")]))
show("R3. HDFC 15-char numeric remark credit (unchanged behaviour)",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("SOME NARRATION", 900, "CREDIT", remark="000000000001234")]))
show("R4. HDFC bare numeric narration on CURRENT account (no SALARY)",
     run("HDFC", "CURRENT", [txn("123456", 45000, "CREDIT", remark="X1")]))
show("R5. HDFC matching debit+credit pair, non-rail narration -> AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE",
     run("HDFC", "SAVING", [txn("ACH D- SOMETHING LTD", 8000, "DEBIT", remark="a"),
                            txn("ACH D- SOMETHING LTD", 8000, "CREDIT", remark="b")]))
show("R6. ICICI BIL/INFT five-field reference (index 4 path)",
     run("ICICI", "SAVING", [txn("BIL/INFT/12345/REMARKS/ANIL ELECTRICALS", 3000, "DEBIT", remark="r")]))
show("R7. ICICI BIL/ONL bill payment (index 3 path)",
     run("ICICI", "SAVING", [txn("BIL/ONL/12345/BESCOM BANGALORE", 3000, "DEBIT", remark="r")]))
show("R8. ICICI ordinary MMT/IMPS transfer",
     run("ICICI", "SAVING", [txn("MMT/IMPS/123456789/Payment/JOHN DOE/HDFC", 3000, "DEBIT", remark="r")]))

import sys, pandas as pd
sys.path.insert(0, '/app/categorizationapp')
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts import AppUtil
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.Purpose import purpose
from categorizationapp.UtilityScripts.CleanName import clean_names
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions

FN = {"HDFC": categorize_HDFC_transactions, "ICICI": categorize_ICICI_transactions}


def txn(desc, amount, ttype, remark="", date="05/01/2022", bal=100000):
    return {"description": desc, "amount": amount, "type": ttype, "remark": remark,
            "transactionDate": date, "balanceAfterTransaction": bal}


def run(name, bank, acc_type, rows):
    t = AppUtil.clean_input_df(pd.json_normalize(rows))
    t = FN[bank](t, acc_type)
    t = purpose(t, acc_type)
    t = clean_names(t, acc_type, bank)
    print("== " + name)
    for _, r in t.iterrows():
        print("   %-46s %-7s cat=%-22s sub=%-12s party=%r"
              % (r.description[:46], r.type, r.transactionCategory,
                 r.transactionSubcategory, r.partyName))


CASES = [
    # --- the five reported situations ---
    ("1 HDFC all-numeric ref credit", "HDFC", "SAVING",
     [txn("SOME NARRATION WITHOUT KEYWORDS", 25000, "CREDIT", remark="0000000000012345")]),
    ("2 HDFC bare numeric narration salary", "HDFC", "SAVING",
     [txn("123456", 45000, "CREDIT", remark="X1")]),

todos.content: Fix HDFC cheque-deposit remark rule (all-numeric ref length boundary)
Fix HDFC salary sub-tag for bare-numeric narration (accountType literal)
Fix HDFC offsetting-credit REVERSAL vs AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE (shift offset)
Fix ICICI TRFR TO/FROM party name (capture-group index)
Fix ICICI 4-field BIL/INFT slash reference payee (field offset)
Verify all five with synthetic single-row reproductions and check no regressions

steps.message:
All five reported situations traced to five one-token faults in two bank rule sets. Money handling was never involved — only the derived label.

## Root causes and fixes

**`BankScripts/HDFC.py`**

1. **All-numeric reference credit read as a generic transfer** (line 100) — `remark.str.len().eq(15)` combined with `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}`, which needs 16 characters. The rule was unsatisfiable, so those credits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Changed to `.eq(16)`, matching this file's own model of HDFC's 16-char reference field (lines 214-215: `^N[0-9]{15}$`, `^[0-9]{16}$`).
2. **Salary sub-tag lost on bare numeric narration** (line 124) — guarded on `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the account type value used everywhere else in the codebase (Controller, `Purpose.py`, ICICI) is `"SAVING"`, so the rule never fired. Changed to `"SAVING"`.
3. **Offsetting credit recorded as a bounce instead of a reversal** (line 98) — the `REVERSAL` rule compared `description.eq(description.shift(2))` while the rest of the rule looks one row back, so it never matched and the row fell to the `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE` rule beneath it. Changed to `shift(1)`. The byte-identical rules in `ICICI.py:49` and `Saraswat.py:20` confirm `shift(1)` is correct; HDFC was the only outlier.

**`BankScripts/ICICI.py`**

4. **Leading direction word narration** (line 159) — `py_extract(..., "TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` took the direction group, so party name came back as `"From"` or was blanked by the later 1-2 letter cleanup. Changed to `index=1` (the name group).
5. **Four-field slash reference bill transfer** (line 147) — `sep_by_(description,2,3)` lifted the third of four fields (the numeric reference). Name is the final field, as in the sibling 5-field rules. Changed to `(3,4)`.

## Verification
- Reproduced each fault on a synthetic row, then diffed full pipeline output (bank script → `purpose` → `clean_names`) before vs. after. Pre-fix output matched the reports exactly, including `party='From'`, `party=''` and `party='12345'`.
- Regression sweeps of 1,140 HDFC rows (19 narrations × 10 remark shapes × both directions × 3 account types) and 1,444 ICICI/HDFC rows: **the only diffs are the five reported situations**. 15-char, 17-char, non-zero-prefixed and alphanumeric remarks, all DEBIT rows, `CURRENT`/`OVER_DRAFT` accounts, and every other narration form are byte-identical.
- Smoke-tested all 35 banks × 3 account types through the HTTP endpoint: no failures.

One unrelated pre-existing issue surfaced during testing (not touched): `SalaryDetection.py` raises on single-row payloads and leaves a `dateSal` Period column behind when no salary is detected, which can make `to_json` fail. Say the word if you want that looked at separately.
